c. Issue any other appropriate writ or order of direction as this Hon'ble Court deems it appropriate in the admitted facts and circumstances of the case to secure the ends of justice.
d. Award the cost of this proceedings.
2.
The petitioner who is the owner of land bearing Sy.No.21 measuring 4 acres 30 guntas of V.G.Doddi, Nayakanapalya Village, Madbal Hobli, Magadi Taluk, Ramanagara District.

The respondents, having come up with a project for providing potable water to the persons living in Magadi Town, the respondents identified a portion of the land of the petitioners in Sy.No.21 measuring 100 feet x 100 feet to construct a pump house and underground water storage tanks and had approached the petitioner to hand over the same, promising to make available 30 x 40 feet site to the petitioner as also provide employment to the son of the petitioner.

It is on the said promise,
the petitioner has handed over the possession of the property earmarked in the 100 x 100 site measuring 10,000 square feet to respondent No.4.

Despite the said handover having been made in the year 1995 and respondent No.4 having passed a resolution on 13.03.1995 resolving to allot a site 30 x 40 feet, the same was not allotted nor was employment provided to the son of the petitioner.
3.

Subsequently unilaterally, respondent No.4 registered a sale deed measuring 10 feet x 15 feet assuring that the balance of 30 feet x 35 feet would be allotted to the petitioner upon identification and it is in that background that the Chief Commissioner of respondent No.4 is stated to have prevailed upon the petitioner to execute a gift deed on 26.09.2001 in favour of respondent No.4 as regards 10,000 square feet.

Thereafter, the petitioner has been following up with the respondents for both the allotment of the balance site as also for providing of an employment to the petitioner's son, which was not acceded too.
4. Various representations have been submitted by the petitioner.
Respondent No.4 in its meeting on 29.01.2013 had also resolved to allot a site measuring 30 feet x 35 feet which was also not implemented.
There appears to be various correspondences which have been exchanged between the respondents interse as regards the allotment of the aforesaid site, but nothing has happened till now.
It is in that background, the petitioner is before this Court seeking for the aforesaid reliefs.

5. Sri.Rajendra, learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that it is only on the basis of the representation which has been made by respondent Nos.4 and its officers that the petitioner firstly handed over the possession of his land for the purpose of the project and thereafter executed a gift deed.

The gift deed being conditional upon, the promises held out by respondent No.4, the said condition not having been fulfilled, the above petition is required to be allowed by directing the respondents to acquire the property in terms of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'the Act') and make payment of compensation calculated as on today for the said land since the petitioner has not C.Mallanna vs State Of Karnataka on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92618509/
4 derived any benefits.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: When the matter was argued on 11.04.2023, the counsel for respondents was called upon to enquire and make his submission as to whether an allotment of site for the balance area would be made.

Today, Sri.A.V.Gangadharappa, learned counsel for respondent No.4 submits that respondent No.4/Chief Officer has expressed his helplessness in allotting the said site and the matter pending before this Court, the directions passed by this Court would be abided by respondent No.4.

7. Heard Sri. Rajendra S., learned counsel for the petitioners, Smt. A.R.Sharadamba, learned Additional Government Advocate for respondent Nos.1 to 3, Sri. A.V.Gangadharappa, learned counsel for respondent No.4 and perused the papers.
8.

This is a rather shocking case, where an officer of the State has promised the petitioner employment for his son as also allotment of a site, which has been followed up by two resolutions by respondent No.4.

The first resolution approved the allotment of a site measuring 30 x 40 feet and the second resolution approved the allotment of a site measuring 30 x 35 feet on account of an earlier site measuring 10 x 15 feet having been allotted to the petitioner.
9. Despite the said promise being held out and despite the resolutions having been passed, the petitioner has been made to run from pillar to post.

The promise which had been held out in respect of a son of the petitioner for employment has not been fulfilled, the said son of the petitioner has also got age barred for any government employment, and therefore, he has also lost that opportunity.
10.

The submission made in that regard is that no direct employment could be made by the municipality without an applicant applying for the said post when an application is invited for and that the promise made in this regard is unauthorized.

The present matter stands on a different footing inasmuch as a promise having been held out that employment would be provided, it was for the authorities to fulfill the said promise, or if the promise was made by a person who was not authorized to do so, action was required to be taken against such a person.

It is not for the authorities, like respondent No.4 to make empty promises and mislead citizens of the country to hand over possession of land, on the basis of promises made by the officials of respondent No.4.
In this regard, suitable action would have to be taken by respondent No.1 against the persons who have made such a promise if he is not authorized to do so.

Insofar as the land is concerned, the resolution makes it clear that it is only on the basis of the promise held out that a 30 x 40 site would be handed over in the urban agglomeration that the petitioner surrendered his land for the purpose of a public project.

If not for such a promise made,
the petitioner would not have handed over the said land.

Having done so, it was for the respondent authority to have honoured their commitment and implement the resolution and thereupon allot a site measuring 30 x 40 feet instead of doing so, a site measuring 10 x 15 feet has been allotted and C.Mallanna vs State Of Karnataka on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92618509/
5
the respondents have kept quiet.

In that view of the matter, the land which has been surrendered by the petitioner would have been required to be handed over to the petitioner since the respondents have not complied with their obligation of allotting a site measuring 30 x 40 feet, which was a condition for the gift.

12. Insofar as the same is concerned, Sri.A.V.Gangadharappa, learned counsel for respondent No.4 would submit that the said land has already been utilized for the purpose of setting up of a pump house - 11 - and if the land were to be ordered to be returned to the petitioner, the interest of the general public would suffer.

If not for this submission, this Court would have directed to hand back the land of the petitioner and returned it to the petitioner on account of respondent No.4 not having complied with its obligatory promises and obligations as also complied with the resolution passed.

13. Since the land has been put to use for a public purpose and the interest of public would suffer,
there being no acquisition proceedings which has been initiated, and the entire handover of the land was on the basis of a promise made for allotment of site which has not been complied with The land cannot be said to have been acquired or said to be in valid possession of respondent No.4

, it is for that reason I am of the considered opinion that the interest of justice would be served if the respondents were directed to cause the acquisition of the said land measuring 10,000 square feet of the petitioner as on today in terms of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and make payment of - 12 - compensation thereof as on today's date to the petitioner.

sentences.text:
As such, I pass the following:
ORDER i.
The petition is partly allowed, in view of respondent No.4 having expressed helplessness to allot a site measuring 30 x 35 feet as enquired on 11.04.2023 the alternate relief is granted.

ii. The respondents are directed to acquire the land of the petitioner measuring 10,000 square feet in terms of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 within a period of three months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order and make payment of compensation within a period of two months thereafter.
Sd/-
